description.short: Dan Cong with the aroma of yellow gardenia — one of the oldest recognized Fenghuang xiangxing
description.overview: Regarded as one of the historically foundational, earliest officially classified Dan Cong aroma types alongside Mi Lan Xiang — serving as an archetype for the category.
description.aroma: Floral, reminiscent of gardenia blossoms, with a honeyed undertone
description.taste: Rich, sweet-floral, with a full, satisfying body
description.processing: Classic Dan Cong craft: withering → shaking → kill-green → rolling → baking/roasting

history.origin: Named after its aromatic resemblance to the blossom of yellow gardenia (Huang Zhi), native to southern China.
history.development: One of the earliest officially documented aroma types of Phoenix Mountain, recorded in local Chaozhou tea classifications.
history.modern: Alongside Mi Lan Xiang, it is considered one of the benchmark Dan Cong aroma styles against which newer and rarer selections are measured.
interestingFacts: Some tea scholars believe that Mi Lan Xiang historically derived from the Huang Zhi Xiang lineage, though today both are cultivated and classified as distinct varieties.
